analysis: The trial completed successfully but reduced authoritative host macro validation HR@10 to 0.4463, versus 0.5025 previously and the 0.505 baseline. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.505, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.535, Electronics 0.435, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.310. Movies improved slightly from the reported previous 0.500 but remained below its reported baseline 0.580. Uniform transition weighting with equal total weight per prefix did not improve the overall objective; these results do not establish why performance declined. GPU allocation consumed 983.10 seconds. No test metrics were available.
code_summary: Trains one independent SASRec per category and loads one selected checkpoint per route. Each network uses 64-dimensional tied item embeddings, jointly trained item bias, learned positions, two causal attention blocks with one head, dropout 0.5, and maximum sequence length 128. The experiment replaces exponential transition discounting with uniform nonpadding weights normalized to 1/batch_size per prefix. Training retains positive-first sampled cross-entropy with 99 negatives, float32 scoring in checkpointed 512-position chunks, AdamW, AMP, gradient clipping, seed 42, and the environment-controlled 200-epoch default. Validation every five epochs selects a single best checkpoint with 40-epoch patience. The generated predictor reconstructs the same architecture and scoring. No ensembles or separately fitted scorers are used.
